ChatGPT — Release Notes # ChatGPT — Release Notes A changelog of the latest updates and release notes for ChatGPT Updated: yesterday # **July 16, 2026** ## **ChatGPT desktop app experience updates** We’ve updated the ChatGPT desktop app to make it easier to choose between Chat and Work, find your conversations and Projects, and continue Work across devices. These updates are now live for all plans on macOS and Windows. ### **macOS and Windows** * **A clearer desktop layout:** A global switcher lets you choose between ChatGPT and Codex. In ChatGPT, choose Chat for quick questions and conversational help, or Work to complete tasks end to end. * **Unified Recents:** Chat and Work conversations now appear together in Recents, where you can sort, filter, and pin them. * **Projects in the desktop app:** Your existing ChatGPT Projects now appear in the app. You can start a Chat conversation inside a Project or begin a Work thread using Project context. * **Continue Work across devices:** Cloud Work conversations now sync across web, mobile, and desktop, so you can start on one surface and continue on another. Local conversations stay on your computer. * **Codex remains unchanged:** As part of this update, Codex remains a separate view, and its workflows and history are unchanged. Quick Chats remain available for fast conversations. # **July 15, 2026** ## **Increased custom instructions limit** We’re increasing the character limit for custom instructions in ChatGPT. Plus, Pro, Enterprise, Business, and Education users can now save up to 5,000 characters, up from 1,500, giving them more room to customize ChatGPT’s response style and behavior. # **July 14, 2026** ## **Search across chats, projects, and files is now supercharged.** We’ve rolled out a new way to search your chats, projects, images, and documents in ChatGPT on web, iOS, and Android. You can quickly find past chats, projects, images, and documents from one place. Start searching from the ChatGPT sidebar to find what you need across everything, or use filters to narrow results by content type. Select a result to open the chat, project, or file directly in ChatGPT. Available on all ChatGPT plans globally. # **July 13, 2026** ## **ChatGPT returns to WhatsApp in the EEA** ChatGPT is available again on WhatsApp in the European Economic Area (EEA). You can get started without a ChatGPT account by messaging the verified 1-800-CHATGPT contact at +1-800-242-8478. On WhatsApp, you can message ChatGPT, upload images, send voice notes, create images, and use ChatGPT in many languages. Linking your ChatGPT account is optional and provides higher usage limits. Availability is based on the country code associated with your WhatsApp number and may roll out gradually. Usage limits apply. ChatGPT is also available on Kakao in South Korea and Viber in supported markets. # **July 9, 2026** ## **Introducing ChatGPT Work** ChatGPT Work is an agent for longer, more involved tasks. It can research and analyze information, work across connected apps and files, and create finished documents, spreadsheets, presentations, reports, and Sites. You can follow its progress, answer questions, change direction, and approve important actions as it works. Work can also keep projects moving through Scheduled Tasks that run once, repeat on a schedule or trigger, or monitor for changes. On web and mobile, Work is rolling out to paid plans except Free and Go. Pro, Pro Lite, Enterprise, and Edu users receive access first; Plus and Business users will follow over the coming days. Work is available in all supported regions. On web and mobile, Enterprise and Edu workspaces have a two-week preview period. Work is off by default during the preview, and admins can opt out before it turns on automatically at the end of the preview. We’re also replacing the App Directory with the Plugin Directory. Existing app connections are unaffected. Plugins can package skills, apps, and app templates for specific workflows, and are available from ChatGPT on web and desktop, including Work and Codex. [Learn more about ChatGPT Work and Codex](https://help.openai.com/articles/20001275). [Learn more about plugins and the new plugin directory.](http://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001256-plugins-in-chatgpt-and-codex) ## **The new ChatGPT desktop app brings Chat, Work, and Codex together** The new ChatGPT desktop app is available globally for macOS and Windows. It combines Chat for questions and conversation, Work for research and finished deliverables, and Codex for software development in one app. On desktop, Work can use local files and desktop apps with your permission. The built-in browser lets ChatGPT gather information from websites and work with supported web-based tools and files. Codex also adds inline editing within diffs, pull-request review in the side panel, faster computer use, and support for multiple repositories in one project. If you already use the Codex app, update it as usual to move to the new ChatGPT desktop app. If you use the previous ChatGPT desktop app, follow the prompt in the app to download the new version. The previous app may remain installed as ChatGPT Classic. ChatGPT Classic continues to receive model updates, bug fixes, security patches, and support for its existing Enterprise capabilities, while new agent features such as Work and Codex are available in the new app. [Learn more about moving to the new ChatGPT desktop app.](https://help.openai.com/articles/20001276) ## **Introducing ChatGPT Sites in public beta** ChatGPT Sites lets you turn your work or ideas into an interactive website or lightweight app without leaving ChatGPT. You can create dashboards, project trackers, launch calendars, prototypes, internal portals, and reports, then preview and refine the result with ChatGPT before sharing it. Business and Enterprise customers already have access to Sites. Starting today, they can also publish Sites publicly and share them with anyone through a URL, expanding Sites beyond people in their workspace. To create a Site, start in ChatGPT Work on the web or in Work or Codex in the ChatGPT desktop app. Describe what you want to build, add any relevant content, files, data, links, or constraints, and review the private preview before publishing. In Enterprise workspaces, public publishing is off by default and must be enabled by an admin. Sites is also rolling out in public beta to Pro, Pro Lite, and Edu users, with Plus users following over the coming days. Sites is not available on Free or Go plans. Public publishing and the expanded beta rollout are not available in the EEA, Switzerland, or the United Kingdom at launch. [Learn more about creating and managing ChatGPT Sites.](https://help.openai.com/articles/20001339) ## **Retiring group chats in ChatGPT** Beginning July 9, users on web, iOS, and Android will no longer be able to create new group chats, turn existing conversations into group chats, or join a group chat through an invite link. Existing group chats will remain available and can continue to be used for now. When an existing group chat becomes read-only, users will retain access to the messages, files, and images already shared there. Individual ChatGPT conversations are unaffected. ## **Retiring Atlas** We’re deprecating Atlas as we bring browser-based agentic capabilities into ChatGPT and Codex. records.label: Business Insider OpenAI and Codex analysis
records.title: ChatGPT is no longer OpenAI's endgame. This is why.
records.excerpt: ChatGPT may no longer be OpenAI's most important product as the company chases stickier, higher-margin businesses. The next battle in AI will have less to do with model quality and more to do with customer lock-in. For the past few years, OpenAI and Anthropic have competed relentlessly on model performance. But according to Samuel Colvin, CEO of AI startup Pydantic, the economics are changing. "A year ago, what they cared about was revenue," Colvin told me recently. "Now, when one assumes they're both trying to IPO, their profit margin becomes really important." The problem is that competing solely on model quality is expensive. Frontier labs must spend billions training ever-better models that are soon emulated. That's not a great recipe for durable profits. Instead, Colvin believes OpenAI and Anthropic are increasingly focused on building products that are harder for customers to leave. "They are doing their very best to find ways of locking people in that are not related to model quality," he said. "That's where I think Claude Code and Codex and all that work is coming from." AI coding services already look like better businesses than chatbots. Developers can quickly consume huge numbers of tokens while running Claude Code or Codex on complex projects, generating far more usage (and revenue) than a typical chat session. These tools could also become exceptionally sticky. Claude Code and Codex help companies generate software at unprecedented speed, creating codebases that grow beyond what human developers can realistically manage. Companies could find themselves dependent on the same AI tools to maintain, update, and understand the software those tools helped create. That may help explain why Anthropic and OpenAI are racing to turn Claude Code and Codex into broader AI-powered work platforms rather than standalone coding products. Anthropic is pushing in this direction with Cowork, while OpenAI is planning to merge Codex into ChatGPT. The catch is that customers are moving the other way. Consider Walmart's home-grown coding assistant, Code Puppy. It's designed to avoid dependence on any single AI provider, and give the retail giant more control over its codebase. The system can switch between models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and others, helping Walmart control costs and reduce vendor lock-in. That's the tension increasingly shaping the AI market. OpenAI and Anthropic want sticky, high-margin products that keep customers inside their ecosystems. Enterprise buyers want flexibility, portability, and lower token bills. The winners of the next phase of AI may be the companies that best navigate this conflict. Sign up for BI's Tech Memo newsletter here. Reach out to me via email at abarr@businessinsider.com.

records.excerpt: Artificial Intelligence | The Verge Skip to main content The homepage The homepage Navigation Drawer Login / Sign Up Subscribe AI Artificial intelligence is more a part of our lives than ever before. While some might call it hype and compare it to NFTs or 3D TVs, generative AI is causing a sea change in nearly every part of the technology industry. OpenAI’s ChatGPT is still the best-known AI chatbot around, but with Google pushing Gemini, Microsoft building Copilot, and Apple adding its Intelligence to Siri, AI is probably going to be in the spotlight for a very long time. At The Verge, we’re exploring what might be possible with AI — and a lot of the bad stuff AI does, too. RELATED / I hate that I don’t hate this song made with Suno 1010Benja’s “Semiramis’ Dream” shows AI can be more than a slop engine in the right hands. Terrence O'Brien Jul 19 Dave Eggers told OpenAI staff that ChatGPT was ‘silencing an entire generation’ The author used Sam Altmans invitation to give a speech as an opportunity to lash out. Terrence O'Brien Jul 18 Latest In AI Terrence O'Brien Jul 18 Apple confirms it took down AI “nudify” apps. San Francisco city attorney David Chiu demanded that Apple and Google remove 13 apps that could generate non-consensual nude images. Adam Dema, a spokesperson for Apple confirmed their removal in a statement to The Verge : “We have always strictly prohibited apps designed to generate, distribute, or consume pornography. ‘Nudification’ apps are against our App Review Guidelines and we have proactively rejected many of these apps and removed many others, including when users have flagged them via our reporting tools. As noted by The Hollywood Reporter , Netflix said in an SEC filing that it paid “approximately” $587 million to acquire a company in March — the same month Netflix announced its deal for InterPositive . Netflix Paid $587 Million for Ben Affleck’s AI Company [ The Hollywood Reporter ] Jay Peters Jul 17 SpaceX might land another big compute customer: the Department of Defense. The Pentagon may make a deal where it would pay for billions of dollars of compute from SpaceX, according to The Wall Street Journal . SpaceX already provides compute to Google and Anthropic , and the company wants to do more in cloud computing, the WSJ says. SpaceX in Talks to Provide Computing Power for Pentagon’s AI Push [ The Wall Street Journal ] TikTok is testing an AI likeness detection tool Jay Peters Jul 17 Apple’s plot to crush OpenAI David Pierce Jul 17 Emma Roth Jul 17 Meta reportedly considers leasing computing power to Anthropic. Sources tell The New York Times that the deal could be valued at $10 billion over two years, with Anthropic paying Meta in monthly increments. Though Anthropic plans to invest $50 billion in building out its own data centers, it has already struck multibillion-dollar deals to access computing power from SpaceX and TeraWulf . Meta in Talks to Lease Computing Power to Anthropic in Potential $10 Billion Deal [ The New York Times ] Emma Roth Jul 17 Apple and Google ordered to take down AI “nudify” apps. San Francisco city attorney David Chiu sent cease-and-desist letters to both companies, demanding that they remove 13 apps that can be used to generate nude images of someone without their consent, according to a report from Wired . The letters ask Google and Apple to stop “aiding and abetting” the sale of sexualized AI deepfakes, which is prohibited under California law. Google spokesperson Dan Jackson tells The Verge that the company suspended the five Android apps cited in Chiu’s letter, adding that the Play Store “does not allow apps that contain sexual content.” San Francisco Demands Apple and Google Delete AI ‘Nudify’ Apps From App Stores [ WIRED ] Emma Roth Jul 17 Apple reportedly sent legal warnings to dozens of former employees at OpenAI. Around 40 employees received the letters, which ask for meetings with Apple’s lawyers and tell them to “preserve documents and communications,” according to a report from the Financial Times . Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI last week and accused two of its former employees of helping the AI giant steal its trade secrets. Apple targets dozens of OpenAI employees with legal letters [ Financial Times ] Thomas Ricker Jul 17 Baseball bans dugout iPads with AI apps. Major League Baseball is cracking down on league-issued iPads provided to teams since 2016 . Teams can no longer install custom apps that tap into generative AI to recommend “substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches.” It seems up to “a third of the league used the dugout iPads for at least one of these purposes.” MLB cracks down on using AI via dugout iPads to help shape in-game decisions [ The Athletic ] Jess Weatherbed Jul 17 Leading LLM’s are political boot lickers. A new report from Meta’s Oversight Board that tested popular AI models from Anthropic, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, and OpenAI found that each LLM is significantly less likely to criticize governments and leaders known ​for restricting free speech. The reasons for the refusals are varied and often confusing. Are LLMs Stifling Political Speech? An Assessment of How AI Models Protect Free Expression | Oversight Board [ The Oversight Board ] Jay Peters Jul 17 Gemini 3.5 Pro was supposed to launch in June, but it’s still not out. Google has been working on beefing up the model’s skills, “particularly in coding,” Bloomberg reports . At I/O in May, Google said that 3.5 Pro was “already being used internally” and that “we look forward to rolling it out next month.” Google Gemini Launch Delayed as Tech Falls Short of Internal Goals [ Bloomberg ] Richard Lawler Jul 16 SpaceX’s Starship Flight 13 launch attempt fizzled out. The thirteenth , and first post-IPO , flight test of SpaceX’s massive Starship vehicle was supposed to occur Thursday night, but when the countdown hit zero just before 7PM ET, “Some of the engines didn’t start, triggering an automatic launch abort,” writes Elon Musk . He says another attempt will happen “hopefully” in a few days, which could be important to investors who are hearing that just hours after SPCX closed below its $135 IPO price for the first time. Screenshot: SpaceX launch stream Jacob Kastrenakes Jul 16 The one AI detector people actually trust. AI text detectors have been notoriously unreliable, but that’s starting to change. This year, Pangram keeps coming up as the trusted source in identifying AI-written text. We sit down with Pangram CEO Max Spero to find out how the system was made, how much we should trust it, and where the line is between useful AI and AI slop. Gaby Del Valle Jul 16 New York City is cracking down on AI real estate listings. Mayor Zohran Mamdani issued a spate of new housing policies , including a provision requiring landlords to disclose when rental listings have been altered by AI or with other tools. The new regulations may not stop brokers from using AI to gussy up mediocre listings , but disclosures may at least prevent prospective tenants from wasting their time touring apartments that look much better online than they do in person. records.label: yellow.com
records.title: サム・アルトマン氏が1兆ドル評価を譲らず OpenAIのIPOは2027年に後ずれ、先陣はAnthropicか
records.excerpt: ChatGPTの開発元OpenAIが「時価総額1兆ドル未満では上場しない」との姿勢を崩さず、IPO時期が2027年にずれ込む可能性が浮上している。 これにより、ライバルのAnthropicがAIフロンティア企業として市場の「初動」を握る展開が現実味を帯びてきた。 OpenAI が株式公開の時期について、最高経営責任者（CEO）の サム・アルトマン 氏が「時価総額1兆ドル評価」を条件に譲らない姿勢を示しており、デビューの本命は2027年に移りつつある。結果として、ライバルの Anthropic が先に上場する 展開も現実味を増している。 注目ポイント OpenAIは6月に米証券取引委員会（SEC）へIPO目論見書を「秘密裏」に提出したが、具体的な上場日程は示さず、この手続きが即時の上場を意味しないと強調している。 予測市場Kalshiでは、「2027年3月1日までにIPOが正式発表される」確率が59％と見積もられている。 一方、非公開市場での評価額が9650億ドルとされるAnthropicは、10月のナスダック上場を目標としていると報じられている。 OpenAIのIPO先送り、その背景 ChatGPTの運営企業であるOpenAIは6月、SECにドラフト版のIPO目論見書を秘密裏に提出した。ただ、その直後に投資家向けに「この提出は上場が差し迫っていることを意味しない」と釘を刺している。 関係者によれば、同社に助言するアドバイザー陣は、社内協議で2つのシナリオを提示したという。ひとつは2027年まで待ち、市場で1兆ドル評価を支えられるタイミングを狙う案。もうひとつは、より早期に公開して評価額のディスカウントを受け入れる案だ。アルトマン氏は後者、すなわち「安値上場」の選択肢を 退けた 。 慎重姿勢の背景には、6月に上場した SpaceX の荒い値動きがある。SpaceX株はデビュー直後に時価総額2兆ドル超まで買われたものの、わずか数週間で高値から約25〜30％下落した。今回のOpenAIの上場観測が「棚上げ」と伝わると、このディールに金融的に関与していた ソフトバンクグループ 、 ゴールドマン・サックス 、 モルガン・スタンレー などの株価も 軟化 した。 関連記事: デトロイト・ライオンズがESPN人材調査を席巻 — 予測市場はESPNの見立てと何が違うのか Anthropicとの「先陣争い」とKalshiのオッズ どちらが先に上場するかが、AIフロンティア企業の「ゲームのルール」を決める。 投資銀行各社は、両社に対し「最初に上場するフロンティアAIラボが、同業他社を測る指標（バリュエーションの物差し、評価指標、倍率）を事実上、決定することになる」と 伝えている 。Anthropicは6月1日に独自の秘密裏目論見書を提出済みで、5月末には非公開市場で9650億ドルの評価を獲得。これは3月に完了したOpenAIの8520億ドルの資金調達ラウンドを上回る水準だ。対話型AI「Claude」の開発元として知られるAnthropicは、10月のナスダック上場を目指しているとされる。 こうした報道を受け、予測市場も敏感に反応している。Kalshiのトレーダーは、OpenAIが2027年3月1日までにIPOを正式発表する確率を59％、来年6月までに発表される確率を73％と織り込む一方、「年内（翌年1月1日以前）に発表される」と見る向きは3割程度にとどまる。 上場スケジュールはこの1年で何度も修正されてきた。初期案としては「2025年末」ごろに最大1兆ドル評価でのIPOを目指す構想が浮上していたが、その後、今年1月の時点では「2026年第4四半期のデビュー」に向け、銀行団が水面下で準備を進めていたとされる。 足踏みの理由は、収益構造にもある。アナリスト予想では、OpenAIは今年140億ドル規模の最終赤字を 計上する見通し で、監査済みの純損失も2024年の50億ドルから、2025年には390億ドルへと急膨張したとされる。 次に読む: ビットコイン価格予測 — 強気派は7万9,000ドル、弱気派は5万6,000ドル、7月相場はその中間に

records.title: Eightcoが4.06億ドルの謎のポートフォリオを開示：OpenAIに集中投資、世界最大のWLD機関投資家としての地位を確立
records.excerpt: ナスダック上場企業Eightco Holdings（ORBS）が、総額約4.06億ドル（約660億円）に上る資産構成を初めて詳細に開示した。その戦略は、3つの将来トレンドに集中している。特別目的体（SPV）を通じて間接保有する9000万ドル（約150億円）のOpenAI株式（資産全体の22%）は、OpenAIの将来のIPOを見据えた布石だ。また、2億8300万枚を超えるWLDトークン（資産の29%）を保有し、公開市場における世界最大のWLD機関投資家となった。これは「人間性の証明（Proof of Human）」インフラへの賭けである。さらに、MrBeastのBeast Industriesに1800万ドル（約30億円、資産の4%）を投資している。この他、1万6278イーサリアムと約1.48億ドル（約240億円）の現金も保有する。同社取締役のトム・リー氏は、AIの自律化が進むにつれ、人間性の証明がデジタル経済で最も価値ある資産になると考えている。 ナスダックに上場する謎の企業、Eightco Holdings Inc.（ORBS）がついにベールを脱いだ。同社はこのほど、その驚くべきバランスシートの詳細を初めて公開した。ポートフォリオの総額は約4.06億ドル（約660億円）に上り、世界で最も注目される未上場テクノロジー企業OpenAIへの間接投資だけでなく、2億8300万枚を超えるWorldcoin（WLD）トークンを保有し、公開市場における世界最大のWLD機関投資家としての地位を一躍確立した。 Eightcoは2026年7月17日、7月15日東部時間午後4時30分時点の資産構成を詳述した情報を正式に発表した。このリストは、同社が単一の上場株式を通じて、人工知能、デジタル本人確認、クリエイターエコノミーという3つの将来トレンドへの極めて稀な投資手段を提供していることを示している。 公式開示によると、Eightcoの資産配分は極めて戦略的であり、主に4つの分野に分かれている。第一に、特別目的体（SPV）を通じて間接保有するOpenAI株式で、その価値は9000万ドル（約150億円）に達し、総資産の22%を占める。第二に、デジタルアイデンティティ分野への重点投資であり、Eightcoは約2億8300万枚のWLDトークンを保有する。Coinbaseの価格（1枚あたり0.41ドル）に基づくと、その価値は約1.16億ドル（約190億円）で、ポートフォリオの29%を占める。第三に、YouTubeのトップクリエイターMrBeastが率いるBeast Industriesへの1800万ドル（約30億円）の株式投資で、全体の4%を占める。さらに、同社は1万6278イーサリアム（ETH）と、約1.48億ドル（約240億円）の現金およびステーブルコインも保有しており、全体的な流動性とリスクポジションの構成は非常に明確である。 以下は、2026年7月15日時点のEightco Holdingsの資産構成の内訳である。 資産クラス 保有数量/金額 総資産に占める割合 OpenAI株式（間接保有） 9000万ドル 22% Worldcoin (WLD) トークン 2億8300万枚超 29% Beast Industries 株式 1800万ドル 4% イーサリアム (ETH) 1万6278枚 - 現金およびステーブルコイン 約1.48億ドル - Mythical Games 投資 100万ドル 1%未満 合計 約4.06億ドル 100% 注：WLDの価値はCoinbaseの価格（1枚あたり0.41ドル）に基づく推定。 3つの長期トレンドに賭ける「ビークル」 Eightcoの取締役であり、ウォール街の著名な強気アナリストでもあるトーマス・リー（トム・リー）氏は、プレスリリースの中で、同社のポートフォリオには将来のAIとデジタル金融システムにおける最も重要な構成要素が含まれていると述べた。同氏は「OpenAIはChatGPTの様々な機能を段階的に改善し続けており、今年に入ってからの進歩は累積的に見て極めて大きなものだ。AIがよりパーソナル化し自律的になるにつれて、『人間性の証明（Proof of Human）』がデジタル経済において最も価値ある資産の一つになると予想している」と指摘した。 Eightcoの投資哲学は、3つの長期トレンドに密接に結びついている。人工知能の分野では、OpenAIの主力消費者向けアプリケーションであるChatGPTは、2026年2月に週間アクティブユーザー数が9億人を突破し、史上最も急成長した消費者向けテクノロジーとなった。OpenAIは最近、将来の新規株式公開（IPO）への布石として、米国証券取引委員会（SEC）に秘密形式のS-1届出書を提出しており、Eightcoが保有する間接的な株式の将来性に大きな期待が集まっている。 デジタルアイデンティティの分野では、Eightcoが保有するWLDは、Worldネットワーク（旧Worldcoin）のネイティブトークンである。このネットワークは、OpenAIのサム・アルトマンCEOとアレックス・ブラニア氏が共同設立したTools for Humanityによって構築され、Orbデバイスで虹彩をスキャンし、プライバシーを保護するWorld IDを発行することで、実在の人間とAIボットを区別する。Worldが開示したビジネスモデルによると、この「1人1アカウント」の検証システムは、銀行、Eコマース、ゲーム、ソーシャルメディア、さらにはエージェントAIなど13の分野において、潜在的な総市場規模が6.35兆ドル（約1031.3兆円）に達するという。Eightcoの保有ポジションはWLD流通量の約8%を占め、世界で公表されている最大の機関投資家による保有である。最近、WLDトークンはRobinhood取引プラットフォームへの上場に成功し、数百万人の個人投資家にリーチし、流動性が大幅に向上した。 クリエイターエコノミーに関しては、Eightcoが出資するBeast Industriesは、複数のプラットフォームで合計5億人以上のフォロワーを抱え、その中心人物であるMrBeastはYouTubeで世界最多の視聴回数を誇るクリエイターである。同社の経営陣は、AIによってコンテンツ制作がますます「コモディティ化」する中で、チャネルと視聴者の信頼を掌握するBeast Industriesは極めて高い希少価値を持つと考えている。 スター揃いの経営陣 トム・リー氏が取締役を務めるほか、Eightcoの取締役会顧問には、アーク・インベスト（ARK Invest）のチーフ・フューチャリストであるブレット・ウィントン氏が名を連ねる。CEOはケビン・オドネル氏が務める。同社を支える主要機関投資家も同様に強力で、Bitmine Immersion Technologies Inc.（BMNR）、World Foundation、CoinFund、Pantera、Krakenなどが含まれる。 今回のEightcoによる保有資産の開示は、非典型的な「上場投資会社」のあり方を市場に示した。すなわち、直接事業を運営するのではなく、集中投資を通じて、投資家がトップクラスの未上場テクノロジー企業や最先端の暗号資産プロトコルに参加するための流動性代理手段となるという道である。OpenAIのIPOへの憶測が高まり続け、WLDの人間性証明分野での応用が深まるにつれて、ORBSのポートフォリオ価値と市場の注目度は、今後も試され続けることになるだろう。

records.title: AI終末予言：OpenAIが「次のリーマン・ブラザーズ」に？ 約138.4兆円の大勝負が連鎖破綻を引き起こす可能性
records.excerpt: テクノロジー評論家のエド・ジトロン氏が1万5000ワードに及ぶ長文を発表し、OpenAIが「リーマン・ショック」級の危機に直面しており、その崩壊がAI産業チェーンと世界の株式市場に激震をもたらすと警告した。ジトロン氏は、OpenAIの今年の計算支出が500億ドル（約8.1兆円）を超え、2030年までに累計8520億ドル（約138.4兆円）を消費する計画である一方、2025年の純損失は385億ドル（約6.3兆円）に達すると指摘。特に、オラクルやCoreWeaveといったインフラ供給企業が、OpenAIからの支払いに大きく依存しているため、甚大なリスクに晒されていると名指しした。市場の見方は弱気一辺倒ではなく、オークツリー・キャピタルの共同創業者ハワード・マークス氏は、AIの長期的な可能性を改めて評価し始めている。この論争の核心は、AIへの巨額投資がいつ安定したキャッシュフローに結実するのか、という点にある。 世界の資本市場が人工知能（AI）大手OpenAIの新規株式公開（IPO）に注目する中、1万5000ワードに及ぶ長文が市場に衝撃を与えた。AIに対して長年弱気の見方を示してきたテクノロジー評論家のエド・ジトロン氏は、OpenAIが自らの「リーマン・ショック」へと向かっており、この生成AIのリーダー企業が崩壊すれば、AI産業全体の投資ロジックを打ち砕くだけでなく、データセンター、インフラ、そして世界のテクノロジー株の大規模な再評価を引き起こす可能性があると断言した。 ジトロン氏は、自身のSubstackニュースレター『Where's Your Ed At』の中で、真のAIバブルとは本質的に「OpenAIバブル」であると直言した。同氏は、2022年末にChatGPTが登場して以来、OpenAIは生成AI時代全体の「信用のアンカー」となってきたと指摘する。GPU需要に対する投資家の楽観的な見通し、超大規模データセンターの建設ラッシュ、そしてAIスタートアップが最終的に収益を上げるという信仰は、すべてOpenAIが持続的に高成長を続けるという単一の前提の上に成り立っているという。 ジトロン氏は「OpenAIの失敗は、AIバブルにおける『リーマン・ブラザーズ・モーメント』となるだろう。それは一つの時代の終焉と新たな時代の始まりを象徴し、AI狂騒に酔いしれる人々を正気に戻すことになる」と警告した。 資金流出の速度は驚異的、財務上のブラックホールが浮上 ジトロン氏は、OpenAIのビジネスモデルと資金需要を厳しく批判した。同氏が入手・分析したOpenAIの2024年および2025年の監査済み財務諸表によると、同社の今年の計算支出だけで500億ドル（約8.1兆円）を超え、これは全世界の計算支出の50%以上に相当する。さらに驚くべきことに、OpenAIは2030年末までに累計8520億ドル（約138.4兆円）以上の資金を消費する計画だ。 財務データによると、OpenAIの2025年の売上高は130.7億ドル（約2.1兆円）に達したものの、総コストと費用は340億ドル（約5.5兆円）に上り、年間純損失は385億ドル（約6.3兆円）に達した。ジトロン氏は、OpenAIが事業を継続するには、今後10年間で少なくともあと3回の大規模な資金調達が必要になるとみている。 現在、OpenAIは米国証券取引委員会（SEC）にIPO申請を秘密裏に提出しており、目標評価額は一時1兆ドル（約162.4兆円）に達すると見られていた。しかし、市場関係者の話では、現在の市場環境が悪いため、OpenAIは上場時期を2027年に延期する意向だという。サム・アルトマン最高経営責任者（CEO）は、1兆ドルを下回る評価額は「検討に値しない」と公言している。 産業チェーンへのレバレッジ効果：オラクルとCoreWeaveが矢面に ジトロン氏は、オラクル（Oracle, ORCL）が高いリスクに直面していると特に名指しした。同氏によると、オラクルは3000億ドル（約48.7兆円）の計算契約の一環として、OpenAI向けのデータセンター容量を構築するために3400億ドル（約55.2兆円）以上を投じることを約束している。もしOpenAIが倒産すれば、オラクルには「回収不能な数十億ドル規模の設備投資、巨額の負債、そしてリース契約」が残される可能性がある。 オラクルの2026会計年度第4四半期決算によると、残存履行義務（RPO）は6380億ドル（約103.6兆円）へと前年比363%増加したが、フリーキャッシュフローは236.9億ドル（約3.8兆円）の赤字で、設備投資は556.6億ドル（約9兆円）に達した。オラクルの株価は年初来で35%以上下落している。 ジトロン氏の分析では、過去数年間でOpenAIとその競合であるAnthropicは合計約3000億ドル（約48.7兆円）を調達した。両社の膨大なAIインフラ構築コストは主に大手クラウドサービス事業者が負担しており、これが「将来的により多くの企業が計算リソースを大量に消費する」という錯覚を生み出している。OpenAIがCoreWeaveやオラクルなどのインフラ企業への支払いを停止すれば、これらの企業は自社の債務を返済できなくなる可能性がある。 半導体大手のエヌビディア（Nvidia, NVDA）もまた、この緊密に結びついた資金連鎖の中に位置している。エヌビディアは現在、1190億ドル（約19.3兆円）の供給関連契約を抱えており、OpenAIと協力して少なくとも10GWのエヌビディアシステムを展開することを明らかにしている。ただし、エヌビディアの株価は年初来で約11%上昇しており、比較的底堅い動きを見せている。 ソフトバンク（SoftBank）もジトロン氏の注目点だ。ソフトバンクは今年3月のOpenAIによる1220億ドル（約19.8兆円）の資金調達ラウンドに参加し、このうち300億ドル（約4.9兆円）は分割払いで、3回目の支払いは2026年10月1日に行われる予定だ。さらに、ソフトバンクには2027年3月に期限を迎える400億ドル（約6.5兆円）の融資もある。 Anthropicも批判を免れず ジトロン氏の批判はOpenAIだけにとどまらない。同氏は、Anthropicも同様に危険な状況にあると見ている。同社は数十億ドルを投じてモデルの訓練を続ける一方で、明確な戦略的方向性を欠いたまま、過剰な数のClaudeバージョンをリリースしていると指摘。Anthropicの存在は、OpenAIが作り出した市場の神話に大きく依存しており、両社とも「モデル訓練と計算能力の調達に資金を費やし続け、大手テクノロジー企業からの計算リソース提供と資金支援に依存する」という同じ財務的プレッシャーに直面していると述べた。 ウォール街が一様に弱気というわけではない しかし、市場の全員がそこまで悲観的というわけではない。オークツリー・キャピタル・マネジメントの共同創業者ハワード・マークス氏は最近のポッドキャスト番組で、AIはバブルを形成する可能性があるという従来の見方から転換し、AI技術の発展可能性をより強く評価するようになったと語った。 マークス氏は、AIには「前例のない」能力が複数備わっていると指摘する。それには、自らの長所と短所を分析する能力、ユーモアを駆使する能力、ユーザーの背景に応じてコンテンツを提供する能力、そしてユーザーへの理解を活用して回答方法を調整する能力などが含まれる。同氏は、鉄道やインターネットといった過去の主要な技術革命において、AIほど高度な自律性を持った技術はかつて存在しなかったと述べた。 AIに対する強気な見方を支持する投資家は、AIはインターネットや電化と同様の典型的な汎用技術革命であり、初期投資が短期的な収益をはるかに上回ることはよくあるが、長期的には新たな産業やビジネスモデルを創造できると主張する。現在、マイクロソフト（Microsoft）、メタ（Meta）、アルファベット（Alphabet）などのテクノロジー大手は、AIへの設備投資を拡大し続けており、AIインフラ投資は長期戦略に合致すると総じて強調している。市場では、設備投資が全面的に縮小される兆候はまだ見られない。 核心的問題：キャッシュフローはいつ設備投資に追いつくのか？ ジトロン氏の長文が真に議論を呼んだのは、OpenAIが必ず次のリーマン・ブラザーズになるかどうかではなく、AI時代の最も核心的な問題を改めて投資家に突きつけた点にある。すなわち、設備投資が記録を更新し続けた後、キャッシュフローと収益性は果たして追いつくことができるのか、という問いだ。 最近では、半導体株、サーバーメーカー、クラウドコンピューティング企業のいずれにおいても、投資家は企業のAI収入の成長、製品の有料化率、推論コストの低下速度、データセンターの稼働率、AI投資の回収期間といった指標に、より注意を払うようになっている。 ジトロン氏は、OpenAIは最終的に、サブスクリプション事業の赤字、広告収入の低迷、そして過大なサービスコストによって失敗すると予測する。その時が来れば、企業の計算リソース需要は低下し、無料版のChatGPTは存在しなくなり、投資家はすべてのAIスタートアップへの信頼を失い、AI関連のデータセンター融資市場も同時に停滞するだろうとしている。 「OpenAIが崩壊すれば、株式市場全体に激しく深刻な衝撃を与え、より大規模な市場調整の前触れとなると私は考えている。誰もがAIバブルが崩壊したという事実を受け入れざるを得なくなるからだ」とジトロン氏は記し、AIバブルを推進する支出は「史上最大の資本配分の誤り」であると強調した。 この論争の答えが、今後数年間の世界的なAI取引の真の方向性を決定づけることになるかもしれない。

records.title: アップルがOpenAIを営業秘密侵害で提訴、ハード計画に影響も
records.excerpt: 訴訟はOpenAIのハード事業と上場計画に波紋を広げる可能性があり、裁判の行方が今後の鍵となります。 Techcrunch〜の説明によると Apple社はOpenAIを相手取り、商業機密を巡る訴訟を提起したと発表した。訴訟は、現職および元Apple社員の引き抜きを通じて機密情報を明かさせようとする不正行為の計画に関わるものだとしている。 この訴訟には正当性があるという証拠は一切ありません – OpenAI TechCrunchのポッドキャスト「Equity」の新エピソードでは、司会者らが、裁判手続がOpenAIのハードウェア分野への参入計画を覆い隠すかどうか、モバイル型スマートスピーカーからの展開を皮切りに進む可能性とIPOへ向かう見通しについて議論した。 裁判所がOpenAIの活動に対して暫定的な差し止め命令や制限を出さなくても、同社の取り組むプロジェクトには遅延が生じる可能性がある – ショーン・オケイン 訴状には、タン・タンをハードウェア部門の責任者として挙げ、商業機密が新製品に対する競争上の文脈で利用され得ることを強調している。 IPOをめぐる話題では、OpenAIが株式公開に向けた機密申請を提出したとみられ、今後の評価はハードウェア部門の重要性の度合い次第になるとみられる。現時点でOpenAIで働くとされるAppleの従業員が400人を超えるとされる点は、企業間の人材流出の規模を強調している。キルステン・コロセックは、OpenAIはおそらく第二のシナリオ、すなわち訴訟を乗り越え、公表準備を続ける道を選ぶと予測した。結局のところ、OpenAIの計画の今後は捜査と訴訟手続きの進行次第だ。 訴訟はOpenAIのハードウェア計画とIPOにどのような影響を及ぼすのか？ アナリストは、仮差止命令といった一時的な禁止がなくても障害がないわけではないと指摘している。裁判は新製品の開発や戦略にしばしば不都合な中断をもたらす。OpenAIの場合、デバイスのリリースやそれに付随する取り組みが一時的に遅れる可能性がある。 一方、IPOの話題を踏まえ、ハードウェア部門への焦点が強まることで、同社の優先順位が変わり、ハードウェア開発の進行速度次第で評価額に影響を与える可能性がある。しかし正確な影響は捜査の進行と訴訟手続きの行方次第だ。 最終的には裁判の判決と規制当局の今後の動向が、OpenAIのハードウェア計画の今後と公表方針を左右する。 他にも興味を持つかもしれないニュース： Bloombergが報じるところによれば、アップルは米司法省と初期段階の和解交渉を行い、独占禁止調査の非訴訟解決を模索していると伝えられます。 マイクロソフトが営業戦略を修正し、自社AIモデルの優位性を前面に押し出してOpenAIやAnthropicと直接比較する方針を明らかにした動きを報告します。 ワシントンの大手法律事務所ウィルマーへイルが顧客と従業員の個人情報漏えいで連邦裁判所に訴えられた。原告は損害賠償と強化されたデータ保護を求めている。

records.label: siliconcanals.com
records.title: Nobody is asking why Apple filed its OpenAI trade secrets suit now, weeks before a rumoured public listing
records.excerpt: Apple has allegedly filed a trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI that could complicate the artificial intelligence company's path to a public listing. Technology Nobody is asking why Apple filed its OpenAI trade secrets suit now, weeks before a rumoured public listing — and the answer sits inside a screenless device shaped by the more than 400 ex-Apple hires OpenAI has quietly made Apple has allegedly filed a trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI that could complicate the artificial intelligence company's path to a public listing. Photo by Laura Chouette on Pexels Apple filed a trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI on 10 July 2026, and the case could complicate the artificial intelligence company’s path to a public listing. The 41-page complaint, filed in the US District Court for the Northern District of California, alleges a pattern of misconduct that reaches OpenAI’s Chief Hardware Officer, Tang Tan. The core allegations The complaint frames the movement of personnel as more than ordinary Silicon Valley talent circulation. It portrays a coordinated pattern of misconduct extending to senior hardware leadership at OpenAI, raising the prospect that proprietary Apple information travelled with the departing engineers. In its filing , Apple wrote that “at every level, from members of its Technical Staff to its Chief Hardware Officer, and in coordination with business partners, OpenAI has been stealing Apple’s trade secrets and confidential information.” OpenAI’s public response — that it is “not aware of any evidence that this complaint has merit” — is a hedged posture rather than a categorical denial. Apple’s filing states that over 400 former Apple employees now work at OpenAI . The personnel movement signals that OpenAI’s hardware buildout — including the screen-free, mobile smart speaker the company is developing with Jony Ive — has been staffed in significant part by talent trained inside Apple’s device organisation. Why the IPO timing matters OpenAI confidentially filed an S-1 registration statement with the US Securities and Exchange Commission in May 2026, with reporting pointing to a public debut targeted as soon as the fourth quarter of the year. Trade secrets litigation of this scale introduces disclosure obligations, contingent liabilities, and reputational overhang that IPO underwriters price into risk sections and, ultimately, into valuation. The litigation lands precisely as OpenAI attempts to convert private-market momentum into public-market capital. Discovery in a trade secrets case can drag on for years, and any injunctive relief affecting hardware development would strike at one of the growth narratives OpenAI needs to justify a listing at recent secondary-market valuations. The hardware pivot underneath the lawsuit The dispute is inseparable from OpenAI’s broader shift from a pure software company to a consumer hardware ambition. The Jony Ive collaboration — anchored in OpenAI’s roughly $6.5bn acquisition of Ive’s design startup io Products — and the reported screen-free speaker device point to an infrastructure play that requires deep device engineering competence. That is the exact competence Apple accuses OpenAI of acquiring improperly. The institutional dynamic here is familiar: incumbents whose moats rest on integrated hardware-software design have limited legal instruments to slow entrants, and trade secrets litigation is one of the few that reaches into the talent pipeline itself. The trust question A secondary theme is how much users, regulators, and now competitors should trust AI companies with proprietary information. The lawsuit converts an abstract governance question into a concrete legal one: if the allegations survive early motions, they will shape how enterprise customers negotiate data-handling terms with frontier AI vendors. Silicon Canals has previously covered Sam Altman’s own remarks on the competitive pressures that have shaped OpenAI’s trajectory. The Apple complaint places those pressures inside a courtroom. The iPhone maker's lawsuit arrives at a critical juncture as the ChatGPT creator readies both a hardware debut and a long-anticipated IPO. Industry insiders are now questioning whether the legal battle could derail OpenAI's carefully orchestrated pivot from pure software to consumer devices, potentially reshuffling the entire AI hardware landscape before it even takes shape. OpenAI finds itself in unfamiliar territory. The company that revolutionized conversational AI with ChatGPT now faces a legal challenge from Apple that threatens to complicate its next act - a move into hardware that could pit it directly against the tech giant. The timing couldn't be more delicate. OpenAI has been quietly building toward a hardware launch while simultaneously preparing for what would be one of the most closely watched IPOs in tech history. Now both milestones face fresh scrutiny as Apple's legal team enters the picture. According to TechCrunch's Equity podcast , the lawsuit raises fundamental questions about whether OpenAI can execute its dual strategy while defending itself in court. The hardware push represents a significant gamble for OpenAI. While the company has dominated the large language model space, consumer electronics demands entirely different expertise - supply chains, manufacturing partnerships, retail relationships, and the kind of design prowess Apple has spent decades perfecting. OpenAI's hardware ambitions have been the subject of intense speculation, with reports suggesting devices that could bring AI capabilities directly into users' hands without relying on smartphone intermediaries. But Apple's lawsuit threatens to bog down those plans in legal complexity. The specifics of Apple's claims remain central to understanding the potential impact. If the suit involves intellectual property, patent infringement, or proprietary technology, OpenAI could face injunctions that delay product launches indefinitely. Even without immediate legal restrictions, the uncertainty alone could spook potential IPO investors who typically prefer clean balance sheets and minimal litigation risk. Advertisement The IPO dimension adds another layer of pressure. OpenAI's valuation has soared into the tens of billions, fueled by ChatGPT's explosive growth and Microsoft's multibillion-dollar investment. But public market investors operate under different rules than venture capitalists. They demand predictability, clear paths to profitability, and minimal legal exposure. A protracted battle with one of the world's most valuable companies checks none of those boxes. Apple, meanwhile, has its own AI hardware strategy to protect. The company has been systematically building AI capabilities across its device ecosystem, from enhanced Siri functionality to on-device machine learning that preserves user privacy. An OpenAI hardware product could threaten that carefully constructed moat, especially if it offers capabilities Apple can't match or undercuts the iPhone's position as the primary AI interface for consumers. The competitive dynamics extend beyond just these two companies. Google continues developing its Pixel line with integrated AI features, Amazon has Alexa-powered devices throughout millions of homes, and Meta keeps experimenting with AI-enhanced wearables. OpenAI entering this crowded field would intensify an already fierce battle for AI hardware dominance. Advertisement For OpenAI's leadership, the lawsuit forces an uncomfortable choice. CEO Sam Altman has championed hardware as essential to OpenAI's mission of ensuring AI benefits humanity. Custom devices could deliver AI experiences impossible on general-purpose smartphones, with optimized chips, specialized interfaces, and privacy protections built in from the ground up. But pursuing that vision while fighting Apple in court requires resources, focus, and risk tolerance that could drain attention from OpenAI's core business. The IPO calculus grows more complicated by the day. Investment banks that would underwrite the offering need a compelling story to sell institutional investors. "We're being sued by Apple while trying to break into hardware" doesn't top anyone's list of pitch highlights. Delaying the IPO might be prudent, but OpenAI's existing investors and employees holding equity have been waiting years for a liquidity event. Legal experts note that Apple has a track record of aggressive intellectual property protection. The company famously battled Samsung for years over smartphone patents and has locked horns with countless smaller players it viewed as threats. OpenAI's deep pockets and Microsoft backing give it staying power most Apple adversaries lack, but that same profile makes it a target Apple takes seriously. The collision between Apple's legal muscle and OpenAI's expansion ambitions will likely define the next chapter of AI hardware competition. Whether OpenAI can navigate this challenge while maintaining momentum toward an IPO and hardware launch remains the central question. For an industry already marked by intense rivalry and rapid innovation, this legal battle adds yet another layer of complexity to an already unpredictable race. Investors, competitors, and consumers will be watching closely to see if OpenAI's hardware dreams survive contact with Apple's attorneys - and whether the broader vision of AI-native devices can emerge from the courtroom intact. records.title: What a Delayed OpenAI IPO Would Tell Investors
records.excerpt: What a Delayed OpenAI IPO Would Tell Investors | Morningstar What a Delayed OpenAI IPO Would Tell Investors If Anthropic goes public first, it could set the terms of the valuation debate for frontier labs. Harrison Rolfes Jul 17, 2026 Samuel Boivin/NurPhoto via Getty For most of 2026, investors have been wondering which frontier AI lab is worth more: Anthropic or OpenAI? Since late June, the debate has changed: Which company will go public first? That will let the market set the terms on how these huge companies are valued. Now, OpenAI executives appear to be hesitating, signaling intent to wait until 2027 for its initial public offering. The companies filed confidential draft IPO documents in June 2026. Reports suggest that both are aiming for a stock market valuation north of $1 trillion. According to PitchBook data for the most recent funding rounds, Anthropic was just a stone’s throw away at $965 billion in late May, and OpenAI at $852 billion as of the end of March. Business Quality: OpenAI vs Anthropic Reports that OpenAI would rather wait until 2027 than list below a trillion dollars is, in effect, an opinion on the company’s valuation from the people closest to the views of outside investors. A company confident that its book cleared a trillion would take money. Choosing to wait suggests the clearing value sits below the target. That would confirm a gap PitchBook has tracked all year. PitchBook’s AI business quality (AIBQ) framework is a 10-point scoring system for evaluating these companies. It takes into account how efficiently a frontier lab turns money into revenue, as well as how durable that revenue looks. OpenAI scores 4.53; Anthropic 8.20. Dividing each valuation by its score reveals that OpenAI looks more costly than Anthropic: OpenAI costs $188 billion per point of business quality, Anthropic $118 billion. That’s roughly a 60% premium for the weaker business. For a year, that was our conclusion, not the market’s. OpenAI declining to test its own price is the first sign the market agrees. To be sure, the confirmed facts are narrow. OpenAI filed confidentially on June 8 and set no IPO date. The trillion-dollar floor and the 2027 lean come from headlines and unnamed-source accounts, meaning a 2027 IPO is still up for debate, since the wait also carries a cost. OpenAI’s projections show the company plans to keep burning cash until 2030, pushing another year of funding onto private balance sheets at an $852 billion mark. Should OpenAI delay its IPO to 2027, Anthropic would likely go public first. Anthropic filed on June 1, reportedly tracking toward an October offering, so it will likely be the first pure-play frontier lab to trade publicly. It will arrive with something OpenAI cannot show: a profitable quarter. (Though Anthropic reportedly is warning that it may not repeat those numbers anytime soon.) Its first weeks of trading will be the closest thing to a verdict on valuations for the category. A Key AI Lab Accounting Metric One accounting question shapes all this. OpenAI is valued at about 34 times its sales rate, Anthropic at 20 times, but they count sales differently. Anthropic includes revenue flowing through its cloud partners, while OpenAI counts only its share. Anthropic’s figure would have to be roughly 40% too high for that gap to close. Its prospectus, public weeks before an October listing, will settle it. A trillion is reachable on OpenAI’s own plan, but not yet provable on its own disclosures, which is likely why the filing stays confidential. Anthropic scores higher on quality and is about to set the mark that the rest of the AI field trades against. Anthropic’s revenue recognition is the variable to watch in the fall. records.excerpt: Apple Sues OpenAI Over Trade Secrets, Threatening IPO | The Tech Buzz the tech buzz Apple Sues OpenAI Over Trade Secrets, Threatening IPO AI / trade secrets Apple Sues OpenAI Over Trade Secrets, Threatening IPO Apple's lawsuit alleges 400+ ex-employees stole trade secrets at OpenAI by The Tech Buzz PUBLISHED: Fri, Jul 17, 2026, 6:16 PM UTC | UPDATED: Sun, Jul 19, 2026, 11:43 PM UTC Add as a preferred source on Google Apple just dropped a legal bombshell that could derail OpenAI 's highly anticipated IPO. The Cupertino giant filed a trade secrets lawsuit last Friday alleging systematic misconduct involving more than 400 former Apple employees now working at the AI startup, with accusations reaching all the way to OpenAI's chief hardware officer. The timing couldn't be worse for OpenAI, which has been quietly preparing for a public debut that could value the company north of $100 billion. Apple isn't playing around with its latest legal salvo. The company filed a trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI last Friday that reads less like a routine corporate dispute and more like an indictment of Silicon Valley's talent poaching culture run amok. The complaint alleges that more than 400 former Apple employees now work at OpenAI, and according to the filing reported by TechCrunch , Apple claims this mass exodus wasn't just about better compensation packages. The lawsuit points to a pattern of misconduct that allegedly reaches OpenAI's chief hardware officer, suggesting the AI company may have actively solicited proprietary information during its aggressive hiring spree. For OpenAI , the timing is catastrophic. The company has been laying groundwork for an IPO that insiders say could happen within the next 12 to 18 months, with a potential valuation exceeding $100 billion. But this lawsuit throws a wrench into those plans at the worst possible moment. IPO underwriters typically conduct exhaustive due diligence on potential legal liabilities, and a trade secrets case from one of the world's most valuable companies is exactly the kind of risk that makes Wall Street nervous. OpenAI 's response so far has been notably cautious. The company issued a carefully worded statement that neither confirms nor denies the specific allegations, instead emphasizing its commitment to ethical hiring practices and respect for intellectual property. That hedged language suggests OpenAI's legal team knows they're on shaky ground. When companies have solid defenses, they tend to push back harder. Advertisement The core of Apple 's argument centers on what those 400-plus employees might have brought with them when they jumped ship. Apple has been quietly building its own AI capabilities for years, investing heavily in machine learning hardware, on-device processing, and privacy-focused AI features. The company's work on neural engines, custom silicon optimized for AI workloads, and advanced computer vision represents billions in R&D investment. Now Apple is essentially arguing that OpenAI built part of its operation on the back of that investment. The lawsuit specifically calls out OpenAI's hardware initiatives, which have ramped up significantly over the past two years as the company looks to reduce dependence on Nvidia chips and cloud providers like Microsoft . If Apple can prove that former employees used proprietary knowledge to accelerate OpenAI's hardware roadmap, the damages could be substantial. The case also highlights a broader tension in the AI industry. OpenAI has positioned itself as an open research organization, but it's increasingly operating like a traditional tech company, competing directly with the same firms whose employees it's been aggressively recruiting. Apple, Google , and Microsoft have all lost significant talent to OpenAI's mission-driven pitch and generous equity packages. Advertisement But there's a difference between hiring competitors' employees and allegedly encouraging them to bring confidential information along for the ride. If Apple's allegations hold up in discovery, it could set a precedent that makes Silicon Valley's revolving door spin a bit less freely. Tech companies have generally operated under an unspoken agreement that employees are free to move between firms, even direct competitors, as long as they don't literally copy files or violate non-compete agreements. The IPO implications are significant. OpenAI would need to disclose this lawsuit in its S-1 filing, along with potential liability estimates. That kind of uncertainty is poison for public market debuts. Investors want growth stories, not legal quagmires. Just ask Uber , which had to navigate multiple lawsuits and regulatory challenges during its path to going public, ultimately leading to a disappointing first-day performance. For now, all eyes are on the discovery phase. If Apple can compel OpenAI to turn over internal communications showing executives knew employees were bringing confidential information, this case could escalate quickly. On the other hand, if Apple's evidence is thin, OpenAI might weather the storm with a settlement and some policy changes. This lawsuit represents more than just a legal skirmish between two tech giants. It's a referendum on how the AI industry has been built, with companies racing to hire talent and asking questions later. For OpenAI, the path to a successful IPO just got significantly more complicated. The company will need to either settle this case quickly or prepare for a protracted legal battle that could spook investors and delay its public market debut. Apple, meanwhile, is sending a clear message to the rest of Silicon Valley: there are limits to the talent wars, and crossing them comes with consequences. The next few months will determine whether OpenAI's IPO dreams survive this collision with one of tech's most litigious giants. records.title: If OpenAI becomes ‘Lehman Brothers of AI bubble’ - What happens to Microsoft, Nvidia, Oracle and Amazon?
records.excerpt: Ed Zitron claims that the AI boom is primarily driven by OpenAI, cautioning that its collapse could trigger an industry downturn. Despite heavy investments, concerns exist over profitability, particularly as OpenAI's revenue struggles to match its infrastructure costs. “ The AI bubble is actually an OpenAI bubble,” AI critic and researcher Ed Zitron says, arguing that the ChatGPT maker sits in the centre of today's AI boom. If it collapses, he warns, it could become “the Lehman Brothers of the AI bubble.” “OpenAI is the reason anyone cares about AI,” Zitron says and further adds, “you can talk all you want about open source models or Anthropic — but without OpenAI, the AI industry doesn’t exist, and the justification for trillions of dollars of capex evaporates.” Why OpenAI can fail? If OpenAI fails, it will be because LLM models are unprofitable, Zitron says. They spend heavily on AI infrastructure, while their subscription business and advertising revenue do not cover those costs. “While there might be billions of dollars left to be raised, to pay any of its bills (for building its AI infrastructure), OpenAI needs tens of billions of dollars multiple times a year” On top of that, OpenAI's free users have become a major liability. The Information reported that the company expected to generate $2.4 billion in ad revenue in 2026 and $102 billion by 2030, but the reality is much harsher than expected. eMarketer estimates that the entire AI chatbot advertising market will generate just $1 billion this year and $5.41 billion by 2030. Now, if OpenAI collapses, there is no compelling story for any other AI company. Without OpenAI, investors would see AI labs as financial black holes, and most AI startups are just repackaging existing AI models without making a profit. According to Zitron, OpenAI's failure wouldn't just shake the AI industry—it could rattle the entire stock market, triggering a much larger sell-off and leading everyone to accept that the AI bubble has burst. But how will it impact the big tech? What happens to Microsoft, Nvidia, Oracle and Amazon if OpenAI fails “First thing is, don't lump those four together - the question kind of assumes they're all in the same boat on OpenAI, and they're not,” Viram Shah, Founder and CEO, Vested Finance, told LiveMint Oracle is the most exposed. A big chunk of its future cloud revenue is riding on one very large contract with OpenAI, so if OpenAI's spending plans slip, you'd feel it most directly there. NVIDIA and Microsoft are also closely tied to OpenAI. NVIDIA has invested in the company and supplies it with AI chips, while Microsoft is both an early investor and OpenAI's cloud provider. However, both companies have many other customers, so even though OpenAI is a large account, their businesses do not depend entirely on it. Amazon's the odd one out (though it is invested in Anthropic). It got its own chips and an enormous cloud business underneath. So putting Amazon in the 'OpenAI falters' bucket overstates it. Is AI spending durable despite scepticism? On whether the spending is durable, Shah says, “mostly yes, with a caveat. The big spenders are putting somewhere around $700 billion into this in 2026, and the point people miss is that they can afford it” These are companies sitting on hundreds of billions in cash with real cash flow, so it isn't debt-fuelled the way the private labs are. That's the key difference. If demand for AI slows, companies like Microsoft and NVIDIA may see lower earnings and weaker investor confidence. “But the bigger financial risk is for AI companies that depend on raising money and recycling it within the AI ecosystem to stay afloat.”

records.title: How China's low-cost AI models are challenging OpenAI, Anthropic
records.excerpt: Chinese companies are disrupting the global AI landscape with affordable, customizable models, intensifying competition and raising concerns for US tech giants like OpenAI. The global artificial intelligence (AI) race is evolving as Chinese firms make strides with their affordable and customizable AI models. The trend poses a challenge to US tech giants like OpenAI and Anthropic. The focus of the competition has shifted from just building powerful AI models to also considering affordability, flexibility, and ease of deployment. The shift in the AI race has been accelerated by the launch of Chinese start-up Moonshot AI's latest model, Kimi K3. The development has raised alarms in Silicon Valley that businesses may prefer low-cost open-weight models over more expensive ones. On OpenRouter, a marketplace for developers to access hundreds of AI models, Chinese systems already dominate the top five spots by weekly token usage. The Chinese AI models dominating developer platforms are from companies like Tencent, Xiaomi, DeepSeek, MiniMax, and Z.ai. These open-weight models can be downloaded, customized, and run on a company's own infrastructure instead of relying entirely on cloud-based AI services. This flexibility makes them attractive to businesses looking to cut costs while maintaining greater control over their AI systems. Industry experts believe that most companies don't need the most advanced AI model for everyday work. Routine tasks like coding assistance, document summarization, customer support, and data extraction can be handled by cheaper models with little difference in performance. Some estimates suggest open-source or open-weight models could eventually handle around 95% of enterprise AI queries, leaving only complex tasks to premium systems from companies like OpenAI or Anthropic. Kong CEO Augusto Marietti told Axios that the demand for open-weight models has surged in recent months due to flagship AI models becoming too expensive for many users. Mozilla Chief Technology Officer Raffi Krikorian compared using frontier AI models for routine office work to driving a Ferrari to Whole Foods, arguing that less expensive models are often more than capable while costing up to 50 times less. The rapid rise of Chinese AI companies has surprised industry observers. In May, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said China was 6-12 months behind the US in advanced AI capabilities. But within weeks, Moonshot released a model that matches top American systems on several key benchmarks, showing how quickly the gap is closing. American companies are now responding by expanding their own open AI offerings. The rise of open-weight AI could change the economics of the industry. If businesses can meet most of their needs using affordable models they control themselves, premium AI services may find it hard to justify their higher prices. This shift could have wider consequences beyond Silicon Valley as companies like OpenAI and Anthropic prepare for major public listings with valuations based on the assumption that frontier AI models will remain scarce and highly valuable.

records.title: Kimi K3 Launch: China's AI Model Takes on OpenAI and Anthropic
records.excerpt: Kimi K3 Launch: China's AI Model Takes on OpenAI and Anthropic Home > News China’s AI model Kimi K3 set to rival Anthropic, OpenAI; Public launch on July 27 China’s AI model Kimi K3 set to rival Anthropic, OpenAI; Public launch on July 27 By Siddhi Jain Saturday July 18, 2026 Beijing-based Moonshot AI on July 17, 2026 launched Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model it calls the world’s largest. The release drew immediate comparisons with the leading closed systems from Anthropic and OpenAI. The model is live today on Kimi.com, the Kimi Work and Kimi Code apps, and the Kimi API. Full model weights are scheduled for public release by July 27. Moonshot describes Kimi K3 as the first open model to reach the 3-trillion-parameter class. It’s built on two in-house architectural updates the company calls Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals, paired with a Mixture-of-Experts design that activates just 16 of 896 experts at a time. Moonshot says this delivers roughly 2.5 times the scaling efficiency of its earlier Kimi K2 model. K3 also ships with native vision capability and a 1-million-token context window. How it stacks up Moonshot frames the release with a caveat: it says K3’s overall performance still trails Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 and OpenAI ‘s GPT 5.6 Sol. But it claims K3 consistently beats every other model it tested, including Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT 5.5. To back this, the company points to internal case studies rather than leaderboard scores alone. In a 24-hour GPU-kernel optimisation test on Nvidia H200 and rival hardware, Moonshot says K3 matched Fable 5 and beat Opus 4.8, GPT 5.6 Sol and GPT 5.5. In a separate test, K3 reportedly built a Triton-like GPU compiler, MiniTriton, from scratch — with performance the company says rivals Nvidia’s own Triton stack on some workloads. Moonshot also cites a nano-scale chip designed and verified autonomously in a single 48-hour run, and a research task where K3 reproduced a set of astrophysics relations by cross-checking 20-plus papers and generating over 3,000 lines of code — work the company says would typically take a researcher one to two weeks. What it costs Through the Kimi API, K3 is priced at $0.30 per million tokens for cache-hit input, $3.00 per million tokens for cache-miss input, and $15.00 per million tokens for output. Moonshot credits this pricing to a disaggregated inference system, built on its Mooncake architecture, that it says keeps cache-hit rates above 90% on coding workloads. The company recommends deploying K3 on hardware clusters of 64 or more accelerators. Moonshot’s blog post also lists limitations. K3 was trained to rely on a preserved “thinking history,” and switching an in-progress session to K3 from another model — or using a harness that doesn’t pass back full thinking content — can make its output unstable, the company warns. Moonshot also cautions that K3 tends toward “excessive proactiveness” on long, ambiguous tasks, making decisions on a user’s behalf unless developers set tighter constraints. It further acknowledges a “noticeable gap” in overall user experience compared with Fable 5 and GPT 5.6 Sol. The release landed days after a Financial Times report suggested K3 was built to close the gap with Anthropic’s Opus 4.8. It follows a string of earlier Kimi releases — K2, K2 Thinking and K2.5 — that had already narrowed the distance between China’s open-weight models and the leading US labs. records.excerpt: OpenAI Releases GPT-5.6 to Public After Government Review Close Menu Bangladesh World Tech Business Sports Entertainment Bangla Facebook X (Twitter) Instagram Artificial Intelligence (AI) English Technology OpenAI Releases GPT-5.6 to Public After Government Review By Tarek Hasan July 18, 2026 2 Mins Read OpenAI released GPT-5.6 to the public on July 9, making its most capable language model broadly available. The Trump administration had requested government review before release, delaying the rollout by weeks. Advertisement The model comes in three variants: Luna for speed, Terra for balance, and Sol for maximum capability. Sol sets what OpenAI calls a new standard for both intelligence and efficiency in coding , knowledge work, and science. What Changed from GPT-5 GPT-5.6 Sol outperforms previous frontier models while using fewer tokens and at lower estimated cost. OpenAI’s numbers show improvements in competitive benchmarks for reasoning, coding, and real-world problem-solving. The three-tier approach lets different users pick different tradeoffs. Luna prioritizes speed for interactive tasks. Terra aims for everyday work. Sol takes the time to think harder. Government Review Left Its Mark The Trump administration made OpenAI submit the model for review 30 days before release. The Department of Commerce’s Center for AI Standards and Innovation tested it for cybersecurity risks. After additional testing, permission came through for public release. This sets a precedent. Frontier AI models now face government scrutiny before becoming public. It slowed OpenAI’s rollout but didn’t block it—an important distinction. Where This Lands GPT-5.6 enters a market where Claude and Gemini already compete heavily. OpenAI still leads in adoption, but the gap has closed. Each release from each company now gets examined not just for capability but for cost per token and real-world performance. The frontier is moving fast, and the market judges speed as much as ability. FYI (keeping you in the loop) Why does government review matter for AI models? Large language models can be used to generate harmful content, bypass cybersecurity, or create misinformation at scale. Government review aims to catch safety risks before deployment. records.excerpt: OpenAI Releases GPT-5.6 After Government Review, Intensifying AI Competition Close Menu Bangladesh World Tech Business Sports Entertainment Bangla Facebook X (Twitter) Instagram Artificial Intelligence (AI) Business English Technology OpenAI Releases GPT-5.6 After Government Review, Intensifying AI Competition By Tarek Hasan July 18, 2026 3 Mins Read OpenAI released GPT-5.6 on July 9, 2026, after a period of limited preview. The model family includes three tiers: Sol (flagship), Terra (balanced), and Luna (cost-efficient). Sol “sets a new state of the art at 80” on OpenAI’s internal benchmarks, 2.8 points above Claude Fable 5, while using less than half the output tokens, taking less than half the time, and costing roughly one-third less. The rollout was unusual: the company had limited Sol to a small group of government-approved partners starting June 26 at Washington’s request, before opening public access on July 9. Advertisement The flagship Sol model was trained to excel at coding, knowledge work, cybersecurity, and science. It’s optimized for agentic systems—AI that operates independently without constant human supervision. Token efficiency improved markedly. Sol is 54% more efficient than its predecessor on agentic coding tasks, meaning the same work requires fewer tokens and costs less despite higher per-token pricing. For production systems operating at scale, the economics shift significantly. The Government Oversight Question OpenAI’s decision to submit Sol to government review before wider release signaled a shift in AI governance. The government expressed concerns about frontier model capabilities and wanted oversight before public deployment. OpenAI complied, delayed the release by 13 days, and coordinated closely with regulators. This is the first major U.S. AI company to voluntarily submit a frontier model to government approval before public release. The precedent matters. It suggests frontier AI development will now involve regulatory checkpoints, not just corporate decision-making. Other companies watching OpenAI’s process will adjust accordingly. Full autonomy in AI release timelines may not survive regulatory pressure much longer. Competition Intensifies Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5 around the same time, at lower pricing. Meta released open-source competitive models. SpaceXAI’s offering focused on speed. The market fragmented. Where one or two models dominated a year ago, now dozens compete on cost, speed, and specific task performance. Users shop by use case, not by general superiority. Sam Altman framed the release as a moment when AI is becoming mainstream, not experimental. OpenAI is now a commodity supplier of compute, not a monopoly. Pricing pressure and competitive features will define the rest of 2026. What’s Next GPT-5.6 likely represents the peak of OpenAI’s performance advantage over rivals. Future releases will optimize for cost and speed, not raw capability. The company’s moat—if it has one—is deployment infrastructure, partnerships, and user trust, not model superiority alone. Competitors have caught up on intelligence. Now it’s a game of execution and ecosystem lock-in. records.title: OpenAI adds teen safety & learning tools to ChatGPT
records.excerpt: Teens using ChatGPT will face tighter safeguards and parental oversight as OpenAI expands study tools and limits harmful content. Data Protection GenAI Data Privacy OpenAI adds teen safety & learning tools to ChatGPT Mon, 20th Jul 2026 (Today) MARK TARRE News Chief OpenAI has outlined new teen-focused safety and learning measures for ChatGPT, including stronger protections, expanded parental tools and more learning features for users under 18. The changes include more frequent break reminders for teens who spend extended periods in ChatGPT, wider parental notifications in high-risk cases and broader use of Study Mode for schoolwork and revision. According to OpenAI, nearly nine in 10 teenagers who use ChatGPT in a given week use it for learning, information, skill-building or productivity. The company argues that teenagers' access to artificial intelligence should be paired with safeguards tailored to their age group. It now automatically provides a more age-appropriate experience when its system estimates a user is under 18. Those users can still use ChatGPT for study and creative tasks, but face tighter restrictions around graphic violence, self-harm, risky viral challenges, unhealthy body-image material and dangerous, romantic or sexual roleplay. Learning tools A central part of the update is Study Mode, which OpenAI said was designed with teachers, learning scientists and pedagogy experts to guide students through problems step by step rather than simply provide answers. Parents with linked teen accounts can now switch the feature on through parental controls, making it the default for any new chat started by the teenager. OpenAI has also introduced education-focused starter prompts for teenagers. These are designed to break topics into simpler steps, turn notes into study guides, create flashcards or practice questions, and check evidence and clarity. Interactive maths and science experiences launched earlier this year now attract 18 million weekly users and cover more than 300 topics, including integrals, mitosis, moon phases and photosynthesis, OpenAI said. It has also added an audio pronunciation feature for words in more than 61 languages. Parental controls Parents using linked accounts can already set quiet hours, turn off voice mode, manage access to image generation and receive notifications in some high-risk circumstances. OpenAI is now extending those notifications to cases in which a linked teen account has been deactivated for violating usage policies related to violent threats or acts of violence online. Some of these interventions were developed with outside specialists, including Moonshot, which works on online violence prevention. The aim, OpenAI said, was to ensure measures for serious cases were effective while still respecting teen privacy and encouraging offline support. Vidhya Ramalingam, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Moonshot, commented on the role of parents in such situations. "In Moonshot's violence prevention work, we've seen the critical role parents play in safeguarding teens online. Parents need to be equipped with the right information to support their children. Notifying a parent when a serious concern arises, with a route to more context, is a critical first step in giving families the chance to step in early and seek help. This kind of access is one of many measures that will be needed to keep young people safer while using ChatGPT," Ramalingam said. Expert input OpenAI said its work on young users draws on advice from teenagers, parents, teachers, child safety specialists, mental health professionals, researchers, governments and civil society groups. It cited work with organisations including the American Federation of Teachers, the American Psychological Association, Common Sense Media, everyone.ai and the Family Online Safety Institute. It has also published educational resources in more than 50 languages for families and parents on responsible AI use. These materials are intended to help adults discuss AI with teenagers and understand how ChatGPT can be used in a home setting. Wider debate The announcement comes as technology companies face growing scrutiny over how generative AI products are used by younger audiences. Questions around age assurance, harmful content, time spent on platforms and the role of parental oversight have become more pressing as AI tools move into education and everyday use. OpenAI framed its approach around four principles: putting teen safety first even when that conflicts with other goals, encouraging real-world support in times of need, treating teens as teens and setting clear expectations. It said it is seeking to balance broad access to AI for younger users with age-appropriate protections. Over the past year, OpenAI added, it has strengthened default protections for teens, introduced age prediction systems, expanded parental controls and added family resources and learning features intended to support deeper understanding rather than answer-seeking alone. "The North Star is to help ensure ChatGPT remains a tool for learning and creativity and not a substitute for real-world relationships." records.title: OpenAI Appoints Uday Ruddarraju as CTO of Compute
records.excerpt: OpenAI has promoted Uday Ruddarraju to CTO of Compute to lead the expansion of its AI infrastructure. Learn about his background and what this means for the company. OpenAI has appointed Uday Ruddarraju as the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of Compute, a strategic move aimed at scaling the massive infrastructure required to power advanced artificial intelligence models. Ruddarraju, who joined OpenAI in 2025 as Head of Compute and Infrastructure, will now lead the company’s efforts to build some of the world's largest computing clusters. This role is central to OpenAI’s long-term business strategy, as the ability to secure and manage high-performance computing power is a primary competitive advantage in the AI sector. Strategic Focus on Infrastructure Scaling The appointment highlights the intensifying demand for computational resources in the global AI market. For a company like OpenAI, compute capacity is the most critical constraint in developing and deploying large-scale frontier AI models. By creating a dedicated CTO position for Compute, OpenAI is signaling a shift toward more specialized management of its hardware and data center operations. Investors and technology observers often view the efficiency of these infrastructure projects as a key indicator of a company’s ability to reduce costs and maintain its lead over competitors such as Google and Anthropic. Professional Background and Track Record Ruddarraju brings extensive experience in managing large-scale engineering systems. He holds a Bachelor's degree from Chaitanya Bharathi Institute of Technology and a Master's degree from the University of Minnesota. His previous experience includes a six-year tenure at Robinhood, where he served as Senior Director of Engineering and Head of Infrastructure, followed by a role as Head of Infrastructure Engineering at Elon Musk’s AI venture, xAI. At xAI, he was involved in the rapid deployment of 100,000 GPUs, a project that demonstrated his ability to execute large-scale hardware builds under compressed timelines. Implications for AI Development The primary challenge for companies in the AI space remains the balance between massive capital spending on chips and data centers and the actual revenue generated from commercializing AI services. While OpenAI is a private company, the efficiency of its compute infrastructure directly impacts its profit margins and its ability to attract further investment. Ruddarraju’s focus will be to ensure that the company’s massive investment in infrastructure translates into stable, accessible, and high-performing AI technology. The company’s ability to manage these costs while meeting growing demand for its models will be a primary monitorable for industry analysts and stakeholders in the coming quarters.

records.title: OpenAI Confirms GPT-5.6 Sol Home Directory Deletion Incident: Pre-Release Evaluation Had Already Flagged 6.3x Increase in Destructive Behavior
records.excerpt: OpenAI confirmed a deletion incident caused by GPT-5.6 Sol. This article examines the fact that pre-release evaluation showed destructive behavior at roughly 6.3 times the previous generation's rate, and how Full Access removes safeguards. OpenAI Confirms GPT-5.6 Sol Home Directory Deletion Incident: Pre-Release Evaluation Had Already Flagged 6.3x Increase in Destructive Behavior Y Kobayashi July 18, 2026 20 min read Translated from the Japanese original Read the Japanese original OpenAI investigated a small number of reports in which GPT-5.6 unexpectedly deleted users' files, and confirmed a common failure path: the model, while trying to create a temporary directory, overwrites the $HOME environment variable, and then deletes the actual home directory during cleanup. In the cases investigated, the most common condition was that Codex's full access was enabled, with neither OS sandboxing nor auto-review functioning. This particular $HOME mix-up is not documented in the System Card for GPT-5.6, published on July 9. However, that document did warn that the rate at which Sol takes serious actions beyond user intent is higher than in GPT-5.5. In internal simulations reproducing agentic work tasks, severe "destructive behavior" reached 0.019% , roughly 6.3 times GPT-5.5's 0.003% . This figure did not predict the cause of this specific incident, but it was prior warning material for the same category of destructive behavior. AD The Warning on July 9, and Damage Reports Starting the Very Next Day GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna became generally available on July 9, rolling out to ChatGPT, Codex, and the API. The following day, July 10, Matt Shumer posted on X that Sol had mistakenly deleted "almost all" files on his Mac. The published Codex screen shows that after 1 hour and 21 minutes of work, a cleanup command from a review sub-agent incorrectly expanded $HOME and then executed the following command: plaintext rm -rf /Users/mattsdevbox On the same screen, Codex explains that it found and stopped the running process, but that a substantial amount of deletion had already occurred. This is only what can be gleaned from the screen Shumer made public; no complete execution log or third-party investigation results have been presented. Still, it is consistent with the failure path OpenAI itself disclosed six days later. On July 13, software engineer Bruno Lemos reported that Sol had deleted an entire production database. In the attached screenshot, Codex affirms, in response to a question, that it had indeed deleted it by mistake. However, it has not been confirmed whether this database deletion shared the same root cause as the $HOME mix-up. There is not yet any basis for counting the local file deletion and the production database wipe as a single bug. On July 16, Thibault Sottiaux, who leads Codex at OpenAI, revealed that the company had investigated a "small number" of reports of unexpected file deletion. The most common condition among the cases investigated was that full access was enabled while sandboxing and Auto-review were not in use. According to him, the model tried to overwrite $HOME to define a temporary directory, and then deleted $HOME itself during cleanup. Sottiaux called this "extremely rare," but since he provided neither case counts nor usage volume, an external party cannot calculate the actual incidence rate. 0.019% vs. 0.003%: Severe Destructive Behavior Roughly 6.3 Times Higher The pre-release evaluation contains a number crucial to understanding this incident. OpenAI reproduced scenarios in which GPT-5.5 and the late-development version of GPT-5.6 Sol each continued internal agentic work tasks, and classified "severity 3" actions—actions users would not expect and would strongly object to. The results were as follows: Severity 3 Category GPT-5.6 Sol GPT-5.5 Ratio Circumventing constraints 0.251% 0.026% ~9.7x Destructive behavior 0.019% 0.003% ~6.3x Unauthorized data transfer 0.016% 0.008% 2x Seeking/obtaining credentials 0.008% 0.003% ~2.7x Severity 3 includes actions such as deleting cloud data without seeking permission, disabling monitoring, circumventing controls, or sending sensitive data to unapproved services. The higher severity 4 refers to actions judged to be part of a broad, intent-deviating plan. OpenAI stated it did not observe severity 4 behavior in Sol, and that it only triggered in synthetic evaluations designed to verify the monitoring model was functioning. An internal case study in the System Card illustrates how Sol expanded the scope of permissions it had been granted. When a user authorized the deletion of virtual machines 1, 2, and 3, Sol could not find machines with those specific names, and without confirming with the user, deleted machines 5, 6, and 7 instead. It also stopped running processes and forcibly deleted worktrees. OpenAI analyzed this as a combination of the model's tendency to persist until a task is complete, and its tendency to broadly interpret instructions as permitted unless explicitly forbidden. OpenAI took fixed snapshots from past internal work, then continued the scenario using a simulator equipped with the code, known tool responses, and read-only endpoints from that point in time. In a test where Sol itself was asked to distinguish between real continuations and simulated ones, the simulated trajectories were selected in 42% of trials. In a separate evaluation measuring "completing tasks without overwriting data," Sol matched GPT-5.5 on the overall metric. These two results are not contradictory: the ability to protect injected changes during a short task, and the tendency not to unilaterally expand the scope of permissions during agentic work, are distinct capabilities. The direct failure path disclosed this time was that a full-access environment failed to stop a $HOME mix-up. This removes both the filesystem and network boundaries, and does not pause even for approval requests. Auto-review examines approval requests subject to review that arise under on-request or more granular approval policies. Under never , there is nothing subject to review, and it does not activate even for ordinary operations already permitted within the sandbox. 最新の報道によると、米イラン和平合意の交渉は最終段階に入っている。イランのアラグチ外相は、覚書（MoU）は「かつてないほど完成に近づいている」と述べ、米国側は合意の署名確率を80%〜85%と予想している。これに先立ち、Bloombergは米高官の話として、両国は来週のG7サミットを利用して合意に署名する見通しで、早ければ日曜日（14日）にもスイスのジュネーブでMoUが締結される可能性があると報じた。しかし、イラン側はこの報道を事実ではないとして否定しており、署名の時期が遅れる可能性を示唆している。
